rules.description: Full-body sessions cover squat, push, and core patterns before adding other work.
rules.target_population: Adults without reported active pain requesting general fitness
rules.implementation_note: WHO supports major-muscle-group strengthening. The exact three-pattern choice and per-session order are TrainMind design decisions, not quoted WHO prescriptions.

rules.description: Increase load only after repeated successful sets; adjust to training status.
rules.implementation_note: The code's three-set threshold is a conservative product heuristic, not an ACSM quoted value. Review against the 2026 position stand before treating as evidence-based.

rules.description: A target duration is filled with distinct exercise and timed conditioning or mobility blocks, not unlimited sets of one exercise.
rules.target_population: Adults requesting a time-bounded general fitness session
rules.implementation_note: Block shares and timing are product estimates; measure real completion times before making physiological claims.

rules.description: Use a default target of approximately two repetitions in reserve for ordinary strength sets.
rules.target_population: Healthy adults in a general fitness session
rules.implementation_note: RIR 2 is a TrainMind default, not an exact ACSM quotation. It must yield to pain, fatigue, and user correction.

rules.description: Start most exercises with one to three sets according to duration and recent performance.
rules.target_population: Healthy adults beginning or continuing general resistance training
rules.implementation_note: ACSM illustrates two to three sets for strength. A one-set calibration in TrainMind is an implementation choice and should be evaluated separately.

rules.description: Strengthening major muscle groups on two or more days per week is a long-term public-health reference, not a command for today's session.
rules.target_population: Adults without conditions requiring individualized medical advice
rules.implementation_note: The current app does not prescribe a weekly schedule; this rule is registry context for future review only.

rules.description: Require three successful exposure records before considering progression.
rules.implementation_note: Three records is a product threshold; no direct evidence claim is made for this exact number.

rules.description: Treat pain reports in the previous 30 days as recent for substitution decisions.
rules.implementation_note: The 30-day window is a product heuristic, not a clinical definition.

rules.description: RepDB source fields are mapped to the TrainMind exercise schema; absent prescription values remain unknown.
rules.implementation_note: Movement pattern, localization, review cues and relations are curated product mappings and are not source claims.

rules.description: Use warm-up, main, secondary, accessory, timed and cooldown blocks to fill target session duration.
rules.target_population: Users requesting a time-bounded training session
rules.implementation_note: Block timing and shares are engineering estimates; validate against real completion logs.

rules.description: For healthy adults, strength was enhanced by heavier loads (at least 80% 1RM) performed for 2–3 sets.
rules.implementation_note: TrainMind uses the set range when the goal is strength. It does not invent an 1RM or convert an unknown load to 80%.

rules.description: Hypertrophy was enhanced by higher resistance-training volume, with at least 10 sets per week as the highlighted threshold.
rules.implementation_note: Movement-pattern volume is only an imperfect proxy for muscle-group volume; it is not treated as a single-session 10-set prescription.

rules.description: Adults should accumulate 150–300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity or equivalent weekly activity and perform muscle-strengthening activity for all major muscle groups on at least 2 days per week.
rules.implementation_note: This is long-term context. Current workout generation does not infer a weekly schedule from it.

rules.description: Allocate a conservative number of sets per selected exercise according to experience, history, recovery, and the hard session-time limit.
rules.implementation_note: Exact session set allocation and duration caps are product rules, not a direct numeric recommendation from ACSM or WHO.

rules.description: Use goal-specific rep, rest, and effort ranges as adjustable starting points; never infer an unmeasured 1RM.
rules.target_population: healthy adult MVP; load data may be absent
rules.implementation_note: Specific defaults are product calibrations and need user outcome data.

rules.description: Reduce planned volume when the user reports fatigue or recent high movement-pattern volume.
rules.implementation_note: Exact reductions and recent-load thresholds are product heuristics.

rules.description: Only progress after repeated successful exposure; regress or maintain after hard, failed, interrupted, or painful sets.
rules.implementation_note: Evidence counts and adjustment steps are product rules. Pain remains a Safety Gate concern and is never treated as ordinary difficulty.

rules.description: Resolve goal-specific required movement stimulus before selecting exercises that satisfy it.
rules.implementation_note: Pattern allocations are deterministic product mappings, not clinical prescriptions.

rules.description: Estimated required session duration must not exceed the user's stated maximum; remove lower-priority volume or movements before reducing rest assumptions.
rules.implementation_note: A deterministic product constraint.

rules.description: Build confidence-labeled capability estimates from recent completed exercise and compatible movement evidence; adjust dose one bounded step at a time with hysteresis.
rules.target_population: Adults with recorded workout and set history
rules.implementation_note: Confidence bands, staleness cutoffs, progression steps, and movement compatibility are product heuristics. The estimate is not a physiological measurement; pain remains a Safety Gate condition.
